newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine rebels attack troops despite ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Philippine rebels attack troops despite ceasefire.

text.p: Moslem rebels fired on government troops in the southern Philippines on Friday, two days after both sides agreed to a ceasefire, the military said.

It said an undetermined number of rebels fired on soldiers patrolling Buldon town, the site of a fierce gunbattle on Tuesday between troops and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), which claimed the lives of 33 rebels and four soldiers.
In Friday's attack, two soldiers were seriously wounded while rebel casualties could not be determined, the military said.
President Fidel Ramos on Wednesday ordered government negotiators to arrange a ceasefire and the sides subsequently agreed to a truce, paving the way for peace talks next month.
The MILF is a breakaway faction of the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front, which reached a peace deal with the government in October last year.
The MILF, demanding an Islamic state in the southern islands, was excluded from the deal. Separate peace negotiations between the group and a government panel started last January 7.
